name: Ronny J
notes: The loudest producer in this lane, and the research is blunt about why: "the whole drum bus driven into clipping so kick and clap fuse into one transient" and "harmony is subordinate to timbre — the identity is the saturation, not the chords". Clipping has an exact MIDI reading and this file commits to it: `velocityTiers` are crushed against the ceiling — accents 118–127, mains 110–120, ghosts that never fall below 86 — the narrowest dynamic range in this batch, and the opposite of Clams Casino's numbers on the same axis. The 808 and kick being "one fused element" is `lockTo808` 1 with `bass808.sustain` `staccato`, `distortion` heavy at 0.5–0.8 wet, and short aggressive glides at `glideProb` 0.5. Hats are 16ths with "32nd rolls used as fills rather than carpet", so `fillDensity` sits low at 0.36 while `hihat.fill` fires at 0.7 in 32nds and 64ths. The melodic layer is one dark bell/pluck/detuned-lead motif over 2 bars, no pad, so `densityPerBar` is 1–4, `motifPitchCount` 2–4 and `timbreHint` is `detuned_stab`. The arrangement is the tag-then-loop shape the paragraph describes: a 1–2 bar intro, hook first, 8/8 alternation, and a drop-out to 808 only before the hook returns — `dropOutBeats` at 0.8 over four beats. ⚠ `medium` because the research rates it medium-high: the credits, era and label are firm and his interview confirms method-by-feel rather than theory, but the paragraph marks the clipping and drum-placement parameters `[LOW-CONF]`. The INFERRED parameters are therefore the whole `velocityTiers` block and the kick/hat placement numbers. Harmony is only ever "static i or i–VII" in the research and this file adds nothing beyond that pair. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 914 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 955/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,4] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 966/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.18 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 966/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
